summary:
Most of this week's Claude sessions went to homelab infrastructure: designing a coordination proxy that serializes access to a shared GPU across multiple inference backends — text gen, image gen, and embeddings all competing for 16 GB of VRAM without OOM. The proxy unloads rival backends before forwarding each request and polls VRAM until the card settles. End-to-end latency went from random OOM crashes to predictable ~11 s cold starts.

On the phillipsben side, Phase 3 of the dashboard pipeline is coming together — wiring Claude's own work summaries into the feed you're reading. The pop-os memory snapshot pipeline is live, redaction rules are in place, and the daily cron now writes this tile fresh each morning.

A few supporting threads ran alongside: containerizing kokoro-tts onto CPU to free GPU headroom, sorting out ctranslate2 float32 quirks on Pascal-class hardware, and hardening the SillyTavern ↔ inference stack integration.

highlights.oneLiner: Phase 3 dashboard landed — Claude memory summaries now pipe into the daily refresh.
Daily cron hardened; pop-os memory snapshot pipeline live and writing this tile.
